headline: Google acquires Crusoe's Wyoming data center project for $17 billion investment
summary: Google plans to invest $17 billion to develop the campus, taking over after Crusoe faced challenges with project costs and construction timelines.
details: Crusoe, a Denver-based data center developer recently valued at $30.9 billion, confirmed Friday it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google announced plans to invest $17 billion to develop the data center campus.
Crusoe had initially tried and failed to land Google as a customer for the project. Google reportedly raised concerns about its cost and construction timeline under Crusoe's management.

The project was initially announced last year with Blackstone-backed Tallgrass, planning to eventually scale to 10 gigawatts of power capacity. This deal highlights the difficulties independent data center developers face in delivering massive projects on time and within budget, given challenges like securing equipment, power, and local community opposition.

Despite taking over the Wyoming facility, Google hasn't walked away from working with Crusoe entirely. Crusoe is developing another data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas. The deal to sell the Wyoming site was first reported in June, but Crusoe still raised a $3.9 billion funding round in September.

Crusoe generates revenue by leasing data center space to customers who bring their own GPUs, by renting out its own GPUs, and by selling compute power used to run AI models. Its largest projects serve major AI names.

For instance, Crusoe's campus in Abilene, Texas, is being built in phases for Oracle and OpenAI. The company is also constructing a separate 900-megawatt campus next door for Microsoft, with its first building expected online in mid-2027. Meta is also a customer.

topic: open source ai agents platform select
headline_marked: [[Select is an open-source platform]] where AI agents earn autonomy based on verified task success
headline: Select is an open-source platform where AI agents earn autonomy based on verified task success
summary: The platform uses deterministic rules to check task results against delivery contracts, increasing autonomy for verified successes and reducing it for failures. This ensures AI agents only work independently when they've proven their reliability.
details: AI agents are getting more powerful, but determining when they deserve independent work is a key challenge. Select is an open-source platform designed to manage AI-agent teams, built with Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and Docker.
Instead of granting autonomy upfront, Select uses evidence from completed tasks. Deterministic rules check the result against a predefined delivery contract, ensuring objective evaluation.

Verified successes can increase an agent's autonomy, while failures can reduce it. This system separates the agent producing the work from the code checking it, preventing the language model from deciding its own output's correctness.

For example, if an agent generates a customer quote, a verifier can independently check quantities, catalog prices, arithmetic, and the provenance of source information. This ensures accuracy and adherence to business rules.

Select currently includes an agent organization dashboard, task management, delivery contracts, approval flows, autonomy levels, and budgets. A fictional demo company is also integrated to showcase its capabilities.

The platform is still in early beta, with future development planned for live provider integrations, OAuth mailboxes, and isolated runtimes for coding agents. Further validation is also needed for these upcoming features.
caption:
How do you know when an AI agent deserves to work independently? Select, a new open-source platform, tackles this with evidence-based autonomy.
